rows.capabilities_note: identity.repair is the CLIENT half of CIRISServer#490: a subject-blind federation key row (pre-CIRISPersist#659 envelope, naming only key_id) is refused at every peer it replicates to, and until now nothing told its owner. The card keys on Warning.code, never on Warning.message — which arrives already composed and never localized — and reads the subject from the structured subject_key_id (also accepting key_id, or key_id= on action_url). SEVERITY IS `warning` AND THE CARD IS RED ANYWAY: error would set degraded_mode, and this condition is permanent until repaired, so it would pin every node holding a stale row as degraded forever over something that degrades no service. Severity answers 'is this node degrading?'; prominence is keyed on the code. Scoped to the operator's own roster, so a stranger's malformed row cannot appear on it, and it renders NOTHING when no subject is named — fail-closed on both halves independently. LINEAGE SCOPING ('fedIDs descended from the portable ID') is NOT implemented: MintedIdentity carries no lineage field and the live damaged row has no delegates_to to walk (open question on CIRISServer#490). The roster relation is used instead, and the key_id string is never parsed for it

rows.capabilities_note: identity.federation_entry is the federation-ID-first login surface (CIRISAgent#887), and it arrives SHUT. This tree deliberately had no fedID sign-in option — the original vendor commit carried a note saying so by design, because a long-lived identity on the device is not proof of who is holding it, and entering on its presence alone is a second credential-less door beside the account login. That reasoning stands; the conclusion changes. Leaving the door out rather than shutting it meant the consumers, who HAVE this surface, would lose it on adoption — so the door is here and `mayEnterWithFederationIdentity` keeps it shut unless a real owner session is open. No per-fedID PIN: a second secret on the same door rebuilds the parallel-credential path this closes. The node agrees independently — resolve_user_signer will not sign with the fedID without the live owner session either

rows.capabilities_note: registry.verify is the FIRST surface shipped ahead of its API. No released node serves /v1/registry/lookup, so on every install today it renders the unavailable path and says WHICH unavailable — that is the feature, not a placeholder. CapabilityWire is the wire contract for the whole ecosystem: CIRISServer#499 declares conferred scopes in src/conformance.rs, CIRISAgent is adding an agent-tier field on /v1/system/health, and this is the one reader, written to be quoted rather than reimplemented. Four wire shapes, four answers — absent means an older peer, null means it could not read its own record, [] means it holds nothing, a list means membership — because those are four remedies and collapsing any pair produces a confident wrong answer instead of a missing one

rows.notes: THE GATE WAS ANSWERING A QUESTION THE WIZARD WAS NOT ASKING. clientMode decides whether AGENT-only surfaces and pollers run, and it demotes a folded-but-unconfigured brain to NODE (CIRISAgent#1075) because such a brain 503s every agent poller — the arm's own comment lists `addLlmProvider 503 <- so the user could not configure an escape`. The wizard then used that verdict to skip the step that calls addLlmProvider, so: unconfigured -> NODE -> no AI step -> still unconfigured. The fix that stopped the 503s had become the reason configuration never happened. ModeProbe.brainPresent = folded && reachable, independent of readiness, because readiness must not gate the step that produces it; the poller gate is unchanged. The provisional half is fixed too — setupHasAgent was `clientMode?.isAgent ?: false`, collapsing 'not probed yet' into 'no brain' while SetupViewModel is keyed on it, so Screen.Setup now waits for the probe rather than fixing its step list on a default. Third place this repo has needed distinct zeroes, after ModeProbe.undetermined and CapabilityWire's null-versus-empty

rows.notes: A CONTROL THAT COULD NEVER DO ANYTHING (CIRISClient#23). The login screen offered "Sign in as <key_id>" whenever the node reported a key_id — which on a fresh install is just the bootstrap keystore alias, so the button appeared for users who had no federation identity at all. It could not work even when it appeared: getOwnerHint resolves to null pre-setup one line above the render, and the click handler refused every press without a live owner session. The call site carried a comment stating there was deliberately NO fedID sign-in option here because a credential-less door was a security hole, and the button rendered twelve lines below it. The guard was correct and the door should not have been reopened behind it; both are now gone, along with mayEnterWithFederationIdentity, which existed only to keep it shut. Removed rather than relabelled: a control whose every outcome is a refusal has no name that makes it honest

rows.notes: TWO ARTIFACTS THAT LOOKED RIGHT AND WERE NOT. #25: an Android AAR never contains its project dependencies' classes — Gradle expects a consumer to resolve them from a repository via the POM beside it. This one is published as a bare file and dropped into apps/android/libs/, so there is no POM and no repository, and implementation(project(":generated-api")) could never reach a consumer. 0.5.195 shipped 5,820 ai/ciris/mobile classes and zero ai/ciris/api; every APK built against it died in onCreate with NoClassDefFoundError on AgentApi, from CIRISApiClient's constructor on the startup path. The AAR is now fat, and packaging/check_aar.py opens the artifact about to be uploaded and looks for the class the crash named — the broken release was a BUILD SUCCESSFUL producing a 16 MB file, so neither exit code nor size distinguished it. #26: LOCAL_NODE_URL was a const val naming :4243 at ~30 federation call sites while the app honoured CIRIS_NODE_URL everywhere else, so a desktop client attached to :4343 sent all twelve ordinary calls there and then minted the owner's federation identity on a node the operator had never attached to. The constant's own doc was right about WHY it exists and wrong that it could be constant: which node runs in-process is precisely what a compile-time value cannot know, and Main.kt already resolves it. Now set once by each platform entry point, which fixes all thirty sites without depending on having found them

rows.notes: THE MACHINERY WAS BUILT IN 0.5.196 AND NOTHING READ IT. BackendSupervisor shipped wired to lifecycle on three platforms with 18 tests, and no screen consumed its state, so a user with a dead backend still read "Cannot connect to server. Please check your connection." from an app whose backend runs inside itself — then restarted their phone and asked why Google sign-in had broken, because an unreachable backend surfaces on the login screen. noticeFor() is now an exhaustive `when` over BackendState with no else, so a new state cannot be added without deciding what the user is told and what they can do; verified by adding one and watching the build fail. Three properties are pinned by test: no state is silent, no broken state is a dead end, and "check your connection" appears only on Unreachable, where we could not ASK. The service's startup exception — previously written to a notification and dropped — now reaches GaveUp and the screen. DRIVABILITY IS AN INVARIANT: 61 btn_* tags had no handler and 124 input_* had no sink while /input answered success:true regardless, so /tree now carries canClick/canInput, /undrivable lists what is tagged-but-not-drivable per screen, and a baselined static check fails on new offenders. THE APP IS NOW STARTED BY CI, four times, against the four node configurations a universal client must serve (#10) — every defect this repo shipped previously lived past a green build because nothing ran the app. iOS Swift is type-checked against the real Kotlin framework for the first time (#24), which found a genuine captured-var race in the StoreKit transaction listener on first contact; fixed rather than accommodated by loosening the gate. Chat transcript tagged so automation can assert agent replies (#27). checkLlmConfig logs every path including success (#28).

rows.notes: THE MOBILE HALF OF CIRISClient#28. Android's TestAutomationServer logged 'Server started' immediately after Ktor's start(wait=false), which binds asynchronously — so the log reported readiness it had not checked, and a bind race read as an app fault: one /health answered and the next died with RemoteProtocolError, another night nothing within 90s. Readiness is now verified by actually connecting, and a failure to accept within 30s is logged as such. iOS ran a BLOCKING posix accept() on Dispatchers.Default and handed each accepted connection back to that same small pool, so the loop could starve the handlers it spawned — 'Server started' in the log and nothing answering for 120s. accept() now owns a dedicated Worker. AND THE SURFACE IS UNIFORM. handleInput answered success:true on mobile whether or not a field was listening — the 0.5.197 desktop bug, still live on the two platforms where automation is hardest — so a green setup step could have typed nothing. It now refuses with the same message. /tree carries canClick/canInput everywhere, and /undrivable and /state, previously desktop-only, are served by the shared handler on all five platforms; the pre-flight this repo tells harnesses to run now exists where they need it

rows.notes: THREE DEFECTS THE FIVE-PLATFORM GATE FOUND ONCE IT COULD FINALLY REACH MOBILE. #32: testableClickable kept the FIRST composition's onClick, because DisposableEffect was keyed on tag alone — so a programmatic click replayed a closure captured before the user typed, and Test Connection ran with an empty api key while the field visibly held one. Real mouse clicks were immune, which is why it survived manual testing. Desktop had fixed this with rememberUpdatedState and neither mobile platform inherited it; iOS was worse still, registering in the composable body with no DisposableEffect at all, so handlers re-registered every recomposition and never unregistered. All four variants now match desktop. #35: the iOS server read ONE recv() and parsed whatever arrived, so every POST body was empty and the decode error came back as the response — httpx writes headers and body separately. It now reads to Content-Length, finds the header terminator by byte offset rather than character index, and encodes error replies with the serializer instead of string paste, which is what made kotlinx's multi-line messages invalid JSON. #34: localizedString returned the raw KEY while isLoading, bypassing getString's whole cascade — current language, then English, then the key. English is loaded during init and isLoading starts true, so the fallback was usually already populated at the moment it was refusing to consult it; the first iOS screenshot the gate ever captured showed mobile.login_setup_complete_relogin to a user. The cascade now runs in every state AND THE CONTRACT #31 ASKED FOR. /input acknowledged work that had not happened: requestTextInput posts into a CONFLATING StateFlow and the handler returned success immediately, so three fields typed back-to-back returned three successes and the product answered “Password is required”. Even alone, success meant “posted”, never “changed”. It now waits for the flow to return to null — the apply signal every screen's dispatch already emits via clearTextInputRequest — before posting (serialising, so nothing is dropped) and again after, and a timeout is a FAILURE, because “I could not confirm this landed” is not success. No screen changed. ElementInfo now carries inputValue in /tree and /element, so a driver reads back what landed instead of inferring it from a screenshot, and it is MIRRORED into `text` where consumers already look — the driver that reported this polls `text` and concludes on the first null read by design, so a new field name alone would have closed the item on paper and shown the consumer nothing; their read-back reports “unverifiable: element exposes no text” on every platform before this. startIfEnabled is idempotent on Android as well as iOS — reported for iOS, identical hole in the other: a second call bound-failed and then overwrote `instance` with the broken server, so a later stop() stopped the wrong object and left the working one running. NOT in this cut, and it is #31's fourth item: the .aar still ships no POM or .module metadata, which is why a Compose floor mismatch can only surface as a runtime NoSuchMethodError on a device. That is packaging work and wants its own change.

rows.notes: TWO iOS-ONLY DEFECTS THE FIVE-PLATFORM GATE FOUND AGAINST 0.5.200, NEITHER WITH THE REPORTED CAUSE. #30: iOS's plain `testable()` registered an element on layout and never unregistered it, so /tree described a screen that was not on screen. The gate waited for `input_username`, matched the SETUP WIZARD's field still in the registry, concluded the login form was up, and then got “no text sink is listening” for a form that had never composed; `btn_login_submit` was correctly absent in the same breath, because `testableClickable` does dispose. A stale entry is worse than a missing one — a harness cannot tell a ghost from a live control. Android and desktop carried the disposal from the start and iOS had it in both clickable variants, added when #32 was fixed: one rule, four copies, a fix landing in two of the three that need it, which is #33's argument arriving as a defect. check_ui_drivable.py now fails the build on a variant that registers and never unregisters — paired rather than absolute, since wasmJs registers nothing and demanding disposal there would be a false positive that teaches people to ignore the check. #34: reported as a missing key; the key is in all four of our bundles and has been since 0.5.185. What is missing is any bundle of OURS in anything we publish. Both mobile loaders read the HOST app's resources (NSBundle.mainBundle; context.assets), the .aar has four entries and no assets/, and the .xcframework.zip has zero .json — so every consumer vendors 29 bundles themselves and nothing we shipped said so. They took the node's ciris_engine/data/localized/en.json: a different bundle for a different surface, 3,739 keys to our 3,892, and the 185-key gap contains exactly mobile.login_setup_complete_relogin. The loader was working perfectly against a bundle that was short. Same shape as the missing AAR POM: a component whose requirements are invisible, so a mismatch can only surface as a defect on a device. This release publishes ciris-client-<version>-localization.zip as a release asset (3.1 MB, 29 languages, 3,892 keys) so an authoritative copy exists and can be pinned, and adds packaging/localization_bundle.py --verify to name a consumer's missing keys in one command instead of one screenshot at a time. STILL OPEN and unchanged here: the .aar ships no POM or .module metadata (#31 item 4), and embedding the strings in the artifacts themselves — straightforward on Android, needing a resource bundle plus a loader change on iOS, which is not being guessed at untested.

rows.notes: CHAT ENTRIES ON TWO AXES, AND THE IDS TO SAY THEM IN 29 LANGUAGES (#36, #37). The server stopped returning a message list and started returning entries on kind (what the entry IS) and author_kind (what the AUTHOR is), with relation as the viewer-dependent convenience. The flat self|other_human|my_agent|other_agent|system|error enum was considered upstream and rejected because a channel breaks it: the same row is my_agent to one member and other_agent to another, and these rows replicate BYTE-IDENTICALLY to every member, so a viewer-dependent value cannot be a property of the row. presentationOf() is an exhaustive `when` over a sealed Presentation, so a new kind fails compilation rather than falling into whatever branch is last. Two orderings are load-bearing and both are mutation-checked: KIND IS ASKED BEFORE AUTHOR, because a system entry has no author by definition and asking author-kind first renders “End-to-end encrypted.” as a stranger’s message; and AGENT IS CHECKED BEFORE `mine`, because an own-agent row carries mine=true (same owner) and labelling it “You” attributes a machine’s words to a human. MODERATION IS A DUTY, NOT A ROLE: author_duties, never author_role — a plain member holding a scoped delegation moderates, and a roster founder with no live steward-bound chain does not, which is a legitimate state rather than a bug. The vocabulary is open, so unknown roles are ordinary members and unknown duties still indicate authority. `unknown` author_kind renders neutrally and re-resolves; falling back to person would be the same absence-as-negative mistake as #21 and #34. THE ENGLISH IS NOT OURS TO IMPROVE. Two source strings drew MQM accuracy rejections in more than one language and were reworded; check_localization_sync’s server-id-text refused them — the client renders the LOOKUP, so a reworded bundle string produces a translated sentence saying something the wire never said. Reverted to byte-exact src/contacts_chat.rs and the 28 translations regenerated against it; the ambiguity is real and is now a server-side question. Also fixed: drive.sh read tail’s exit code in a pipeline, so every lane refusal and crash reported “DONE: lane clean” and the retry loop had never once fired. Found only by noticing the work had not happened. rows.notes: A CLICK MUST REACH THE UI THREAD (#30), AND THE FIX IN 0.5.201 WAS FOR A DIFFERENT DEFECT. The symptom was unchanged at .201 and again at .202, which is what said the diagnosis was wrong: a stale registry entry had been blamed, and iOS's testable() disposal fixed — a real defect, not this one. The screenshot settled it: the login chooser shows “Local Login” still an unexpanded button, so the three reported failures (no text sink for input_username, no sink for input_password, btn_login_submit not found) are ONE failure — LocalLoginForm never composed, so it registered no sinks and no submit button. Ruled out rather than guessed: the handler is `if (isFirstRun) onLocalLogin() else { showLoginForm = true }` and onLocalLogin navigates to Screen.Setup, but the driver reported “Still on Login screen after 30s” — so isFirstRun was false, the else-branch ran, the state write happened and the recomposition did not. iOS-only because of what the state IS: SetupScreen drives its steps through viewModel.state.collectAsState(), a StateFlow whose collector resumes on main, which is why the wizard passes 6/6 and why text input works; the login toggle is a composable's own snapshot state written directly by the handler, and iOS serves automation from a Kotlin/Native Worker. Android and desktop serve from background threads too and recompose anyway, so the difference is Kotlin/Native rather than the architecture. handleClick now dispatches on Dispatchers.Main, in the shared handler; desktop's separate server is #33's un-consolidated half and inherits it later. ALSO: the server's contacts plane is now fully covered — 11 ids added, taking server-id-coverage to 0 findings over 321 emitted ids at CIRISServer 0.5.198. Ten of the eleven are emitted through format!() with runtime values, so the guard cannot compare them and the bundle carries what a PERSON should read rather than an operator sentence with a fed-id spliced in; the eleventh is a literal the guard pins byte-exactly, and its “retry once it has arrived” contradicts #37's “do not offer retry” — a server-side wording question, raised there rather than papered over here. node_max_tested and agent_min_tested are brought current (0.5.198 / 2.10.0); they had lagged to 0.5.190 / 2.9.41. THE WIZARD ASKS ABOUT AI FIRST, AND SKIPS THE LLM SCREEN WHEN THE ANSWER IS NO. The question moved from a switch on the LLM screen — where the only way to say “no AI” was to visit the screen that configures one — to screen 1, phrased as a choice. One predicate (hasAiStep) now feeds all four places that decide the step shape: next, previous, which step is final, and the progress dots. They have to agree, or Next advances to a screen that is never rendered and the wizard strands the user with no Complete button. Screen 1 is ordered required-first (AI → age → account → fed-ID), the age bands sit side by side instead of as two stacked cards, every step draws a visible scrollbar on desktop, and an undrivable fed-ID label falls back to `cirisuser` — safe because the node appends a UUID when it mints, so a shared stem is not a shared identity. AND THIS CLIENT FOLLOWS THAT BACKEND. From CIRISAgent 2.11.0 (#1149 / PR #1150) a run-without-AI setup shuts the brain down and only :4243 serves; :8080 goes away. Both mobile runtimes hard-coded :8080 as a constant, so that pairing would have looked like a dead app — BackendEndpoint replaces the constants with one tested function, reading CIRIS_RUN_WITHOUT_AI from the home's .env. Absent means the agent, deliberately: every install predating the flag serves :8080. The port and path are shared and the HOST stays with the caller, because Android must say `localhost` and not `127.0.0.1` (the WebView's Same-Origin Policy treats them as different origins). Two review findings changed it: the agent's own reader also accepted `on`, which would have sent them to :4243 while this client polled :8080 with nothing in either log saying why (they narrowed to match, and the non-truthy spellings are tested here so a widening on either side fails in CI); and 200-means-serving turned out to be SETTLED rather than provisional — /health serves a constant "status": "ok" and "starting" has no producer anywhere in the node (CIRISServer#548). So 0.5.203 pairs correctly with BOTH 2.10.0, which drops the flag and keeps :8080, and 2.11.0, which does not. Handover is guaranteed (a): the runtime shutdown moved to FastAPI BackgroundTasks, which run after the response is sent, so a dropped connection on /v1/setup/complete remains a real failure and is not special-cased.

rows.notes: A RESTART WAITS FOR THE PORTS, NOT THE PID (#40). After a factory reset the next setup could not boot: the backend the app had just stopped still held :4242 and :4243. The agent measured that SIGTERM is accepted and never acted on (CIRISAgent#1152) and that SIGKILL releases the ports ~2s AFTER the pid is gone. Underneath that, our own shutdown never escalated: Process.waitFor(5s) returns false on timeout and the SIGKILL lived only in a catch, so every reset left the backend running. Now one SIGTERM, a 5s grace (kept, not relied on), SIGKILL, then a real bind() on :8080/:4243/:4242 until they clear (15s), and the same wait before any launch, with a message naming the held ports if they never do. Never a second SIGTERM. Desktop only; mobile runtimes are unchanged. Pairs with every agent and node 0.5.204 does.

rows.notes: /scroll ACTUALLY SCROLLS, AND SAYS SO ONLY WHEN IT DID (#33). handleScroll posted to a StateFlow and returned success:true; nothing in the tree collected that flow on ANY platform -- its only references were its own declaration, setter and clearer. Invisible while /click and /input still drove off-screen elements through a coordinate fallback; 0.5.206 correctly made them refuse, the agent's gate moved recovery into its primitives (scroll once, ask again), and the recovery could not work: iOS inert but reporting success, Android 404 (the shared handler existed, the third hand-written route table lacked the line), desktop turning a Robot wheel at an off-screen element's clipped zero-size centre and still answering success. Adds the missing consumer as ONE implementation -- rememberTestableScrollState() / Modifier.testableVerticalScroll(), 45 files migrated, a no-op outside test mode, most-recent scrollable owns the dispatch. handleScroll now refuses when nothing on screen can scroll (naming the screen and what is drivable) and otherwise waits for the consumer to apply before answering, like /input (#31); a timeout is a failure. HARNESS-VISIBLE CHANGE: a refused /scroll is 404 with a reason, not 200 -- retry only on 200. Desktop's wheel remains a fallback for a POSITIONED element, reported as action 'mouse-wheel' so a caller knows which path ran. Pairs with every agent and node 0.5.206 does.

rows.notes: BOTH AGE BANDS RENDERED AT ZERO WIDTH FROM 0.5.203 (#42). 'Prefer not to say' sat inside the same Row as the two bands carrying fillMaxWidth(); Row measures unweighted children first against the full width and gives the weighted ones what remains, so that child took all of it and both bands measured to zero. USER-FACING, not a harness artifact: the bands were invisible to a person, so the only selectable answer on a required question was 'prefer not to say', which is treated as under-18 WITH STEWARDSHIP -- every setup since 0.5.203 took the protective path whether or not the owner wanted it. It hid because the controls were still composed and still registered click handlers, so the pre-0.5.206 coordinate fallback clicked a zero-size rect and automation looked green; 0.5.206's honest visibility reporting is what surfaced it, the agent's gate reading four drivable controls on the YOU step with NEITHER band among them. Adds client/tools/check_row_layout.py, a hard-zero lint in build.yml and the release gates that walks each Row's children seeing THROUGH control flow (the bands were inside a forEach, which is why no direct-child reading of the source put them beside the offender) and stopping at nested layout containers; mutation-verified in both directions. 0.5.207 published its wheels to PyPI but its ios-xcframework job was CANCELLED to cut this release, so the v0.5.207 GitHub release carries no XCFramework -- take iOS artifacts from v0.5.208. rows.notes: THE RUN-WITHOUT-AI SWITCH WAS NEVER PLUGGED IN (#43). After the hand-off the client kept polling :8080 -- 109 CIRISApiClient inits at the agent port, none at :4243, and 'Restarting your node...' forever while the node was serving the whole time. Not an overwrite: :4243 was never chosen. ActiveBackend, runWithoutAiFromEnv and BackendEndpoint shipped in 0.5.203 with fifteen passing tests and ActiveBackend.resolveFrom HAD NO PRODUCTION CALLER ON ANY PLATFORM -- its only references were that test and a doc comment saying 'a platform that has not wired resolveFrom yet', which described every platform. Desktop never consulted it and took its port from CIRIS_API_URL (the launcher sets the agent's :8080); iOS and Android read it and so carried the SAME BUG LATENT, undriven. Now resolved at BOTH moments it must hold: at startup before anything polls, and when setup COMPLETES, because the hand-off replaces the agent process and not the client. EnvFileUpdater.readRawEnv() (expect + four actuals) is the read, syncBackendFromEnv the seam, and desktop's PythonRuntime.serverUrl follows the same answer so the health poll moves too. The node URL is forced ONLY in the run-without-AI direction: the other way would stamp on CIRIS_NODE_URL and on an operator attached to someone else's node (#26). LOOPBACK_HOST replaces two hardcoded call sites -- Android must say localhost for the WebView's Same-Origin Policy. MOBILE IS FIXED BY THE SAME CHANGE, having been broken the same way without anyone driving it. Pairs with agent 2.11.0, which shuts the brain down and serves only :4243, and with every agent and node 0.5.208 does.

rows.notes: THE API CLIENT MOVES WITH THE BACKEND, NOT JUST THE NODE URL (#43, completing 0.5.209). 0.5.209 re-pointed CIRISApiClient.LOCAL_NODE_URL, which the FEDERATION call sites read. Every ordinary call -- login included -- goes through the client's own baseUrl, and CIRISApp builds that once inside a `remember` from apiBaseUrl, defaulting to :8080. So after a run-without-AI hand-off the node URL moved to :4243 and login still went to the port that had just gone away. Found by checking the agent team's forecast that Android in-session login would pass on 0.5.209 -- it would not have. syncBackendFrom now takes the api client as a REQUIRED argument and calls updateBaseUrl, which recreates the ~13 generated SDK instances as well as the direct HTTP path; required rather than optional because this whole issue exists from a function that had to be called and was not, and an optional argument is the same trap one storey down. Still only in the run-without-AI direction, so a with-AI home and an operator attached to another node are untouched (#26). WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS: the agent hosts a node fold on :4243 DURING the wizard, so once it stops ending its process that fold keeps serving -- the hand-off needs no restart and no in-place node boot, and the client only has to talk to it. Android no-AI setup is 7/7 on the agent's side; this is the client half of the login that follows it. Pairs with agent 2.11.0 and with every agent and node 0.5.209 does.
